nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $T$ with transition function $\delta$, and let $\varphi$ map each letter of $T$ to a word over $T'$. For a state $q$ of $M$, a letter $a$ and a natural number $i$, the state reached after emitting position $i$ (counted from $0$) of $\varphi(a)$ from $q$ is the intermediate state $(q, a, i + 1)$ of the ε-NFA if $i + 1 < |\varphi(a)|$, and the state $\delta(q, a)$ of $M$…
nodes.title: Next state while spelling out a letter's image

nodes.summary: For a map $\varphi$ from a finite alphabet $T$ to words over $T'$, the bound is the maximum of the lengths $|\varphi(a)|$ over all letters $a \in T$ (and $0$ when $T$ is empty).
nodes.title: Maximal length of the image of a letter

nodes.summary: For a map $\varphi$ from letters of $T$ to words over $T'$ and a letter $a$, the label sequence of $a$ is a single ε-label when $\varphi(a)$ is empty, and otherwise the letters of $\varphi(a)$ in order, each as a non-ε label.
nodes.title: Edge labels for a letter's image

nodes.summary: The cyclic shifts of the words of a regular language form a regular language.
nodes.title: The cyclic shifts of the words of a regular language form a regular language

nodes.summary: For a language $L$ over $\alpha$, the cyclic shift of $L$ is the language of all words $yx$ over $\alpha$ such that $xy \in L$ for some words $x$ and $y$; that is, the language of all rotations of the words of $L$.
nodes.title: Cyclic shift of a language

nodes.summary: For a word $y = b_1 \cdots b_n$ over $T'$, the detour labels of $y$ are the sequence of ε-NFA labels $\varepsilon, b_1, \ldots, b_n, \varepsilon$: an ε-move, the letters of $y$ in order, and a final ε-move.
nodes.title: Detour labels

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over $T$ with start state $q_0$, and for each letter $a \in T$ let $N_a$ be a DFA over $T'$, with accepted language $L(N_a)$; for a word $w = a_1 \cdots a_n$ over $T$ write $L_w = L(N_{a_1}) \cdots L(N_{a_n})$, which is $\{\varepsilon\}$ when $w$ is empty. Let $x$ be a sequence of labels, each a letter of $T'$ or $\varepsilon$, let $\bar x$ be the word over $T'$ obtained from $x$ by deleting the…
nodes.title: Soundness of the paths of the substitution ε-NFA

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $T$ with start state $q_0$, and let $\varphi$ map letters of $T$ to words over $T'$; for a word $w$ over $T$, write $\varphi(w)$ for the concatenation of the images of its letters. Suppose the ε-NFA of $M$ and $\varphi$ has a path from the state $q_0$ of $M$ to a state $u$, with label sequence $x$, and let $\bar x$ be the word formed by the non-ε labels of $x$. If $u$ is a…
nodes.title: Soundness of the homomorphic-image ε-NFA

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over $\alpha$ with state type $\sigma$, a state $p \in \sigma$ and a set $S \subseteq \sigma$ of states, this is the language of all words $w$ over $\alpha$ such that the run of $M$ started in $p$ on $w$ ends in a state of $S$.
nodes.title: Words leading a DFA from a state into a set of states

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet, $T'$ an arbitrary (possibly infinite) alphabet, and $\varphi$ a map from $T$ to words over $T'$, extended to words by $\varphi(a_1 \cdots a_n) = \varphi(a_1) \cdots \varphi(a_n)$. If $L$ is a regular language over $T$, then its image $\{\varphi(w) : w \in L\}$ is a regular language over $T'$.
nodes.title: Homomorphic images of regular languages over finite alphabets are regular

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $T$ with transition function $\delta$, and let $\varphi$ map letters of $T$ to words over $T'$. For every state $q$ of $M$, letter $a$ and natural number $i$, the ε-NFA of $M$ and $\varphi$ has a path to the state $\delta(q, a)$ of $M$ from the state $(q, a, i + 1)$ if $i + 1 < |\varphi(a)|$, and from $\delta(q, a)$ otherwise, whose labels are the letters of $\varphi(a)$…
nodes.title: Finishing a letter's image in the image ε-NFA

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $T$ with transition function $\delta$, and let $\varphi$ map letters of $T$ to words over $T'$. For every state $q$ of $M$ and letter $a$, the ε-NFA of $M$ and $\varphi$ has a path from the state $q$ to the state $\delta(q, a)$ whose label sequence is a single ε-label if $\varphi(a)$ is empty, and the letters of $\varphi(a)$ in order, all non-ε, otherwise.
nodes.title: Spelling out a letter's image in the image ε-NFA

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over $T$, and for each letter $a \in T$ let $N_a$ be a DFA over $T'$. For every state $q$ of $M$, letter $a \in T$, state $p$ of $N_a$ and word $y$ over $T'$, the ε-NFA built from $M$ and the $N_a$ has a path reading the letters of $y$, with no ε-moves, from the state $p$ of the copy of $N_a$ entered from $q$ to the state of the same copy that $N_a$ reaches from $p$ on $y$.
nodes.title: Paths inside one copy of a letter automaton

nodes.summary: The relation "$w$ is a shuffle of $u$ and $v$" on words over $\alpha$ is defined inductively: the empty word is a shuffle of the empty word and the empty word, and if $w$ is a shuffle of $u$ and $v$, then for every letter $a$ the word $aw$ is a shuffle of $au$ and $v$, and a shuffle of $u$ and $av$. Thus $w$ interleaves the letters of $u$ and of $v$, keeping their order within each word.
nodes.title: Shuffle of two words

nodes.summary: Given a DFA $M$ over an alphabet $T$ with state set $\sigma$ and a language $R$ over $T$, this is the NFA with state set $\sigma$ and the same accepting states as $M$, in which from a state $q$ on a letter $a$ the only possible move is to the state $M$ reaches from $q$ on $a$, and whose start states are the states that $M$ reaches from its start state on the words of $R$.
nodes.title: NFA for the left quotient by a language

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a regular language over an alphabet $T$ and $R$ is any language over $T$, then the left quotient $\{y \mid \exists x \in R,\ xy \in L\}$ of $L$ by $R$ is regular.
nodes.title: Regular languages are closed under left quotients by arbitrary languages

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over $T$ with states $\sigma$, and for each letter $a \in T$ let $N_a$ be a DFA over $T'$ with states $\tau_a$. This ε-NFA over $T'$ has as states the states $q$ of $M$ and the triples $(q, a, p)$ with $q$ a state of $M$, $a \in T$ and $p$ a state of $N_a$, read as the state $p$ of the copy of $N_a$ entered from $q$. A state $q$ of $M$ has an ε-move to $(q, a, s_a)$ for every $a \in T$, where $s_a$…
nodes.title: The ε-NFA for a substitution

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $T$ with start state $q_0$, transition function $\delta$ and accepting states $F$, let $\varphi$ map letters of $T$ to words over $T'$, and let $N$ be the maximum of the lengths $|\varphi(a)|$ over $a \in T$. The ε-NFA over $T'$ has as states the states of $M$ together with the triples $(q, a, i)$ with $q$ a state of $M$, $a \in T$ and $0 \le i < N$. Write…
nodes.title: The ε-NFA for the homomorphic image

nodes.summary: Given a DFA $M$ over an alphabet $T$ with state set $\sigma$ and a language $R$ over $T$, this is the DFA with the same states, transition function and start state as $M$, whose accepting states are the states $q$ from which some word of $R$ leads $M$ to an accepting state of $M$.
nodes.title: DFA for the right quotient by a language

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a regular language over an alphabet $T$ and $R$ is any language over $T$, then the right quotient $\{x \mid \exists y \in R,\ xy \in L\}$ of $L$ by $R$ is regular.
nodes.title: Regular languages are closed under right quotients by arbitrary languages

nodes.summary: The shuffle of two regular languages is regular.
nodes.title: The shuffle of two regular languages is regular

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be DFAs over $\alpha$ with state types $\sigma$ and $\tau$, start states $s_M$ and $s_N$, sets of accepting states $F_M$ and $F_N$, and transition functions $\delta_M$ and $\delta_N$. Their shuffle automaton is the NFA over $\alpha$ with state type $\sigma \times \tau$, the single start state $(s_M, s_N)$ and accepting states $F_M \times F_N$, which on a letter $a$ moves from a state $(p, q)$ to the…
nodes.title: Shuffle automaton of two DFAs

nodes.summary: For languages $L$ and $M$ over $\alpha$, the shuffle of $L$ and $M$ is the language of all words $w$ over $\alpha$ such that $w$ is a shuffle of some word $u \in L$ and some word $v \in M$, that is, $w$ interleaves $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Shuffle of two languages

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet, let $\varphi$ map letters of $T$ to words over $T'$, let $\sigma$ be a set (the states of a DFA), and let $N$ be the maximum of the lengths $|\varphi(a)|$ over $a \in T$. The states of the ε-NFA form the disjoint union of $\sigma$ and the set of triples $(q, a, i)$ with $q \in \sigma$, $a \in T$ and $0 \le i < N$.
nodes.title: States of the homomorphic-image ε-NFA

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $T$, and let $s$ assign to each letter $a \in T$ a language $s(a)$ over an alphabet $T'$. The substitution of $s$ into $L$ is the language over $T'$ of all words $y_1 y_2 \cdots y_n$ for which there is a word $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n \in L$ with $y_i \in s(a_i)$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Substitution of languages for letters

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet and $T'$ any alphabet. If $L$ is a regular language over $T$ and $s(a)$ is a regular language over $T'$ for every letter $a \in T$, then the substitution of $s$ into $L$ is a regular language over $T'$.
nodes.title: Regular languages are closed under substitution over a finite alphabet
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
